manifest.title: PostHog
manifest.tagline: Product analytics, session replay and feature flags in one app
manifest.description:
PostHog, packaged as a single Cloudron app: product analytics, web analytics, session replay,
feature flags, surveys, heatmaps, error tracking and data transformations, on one container.

**What this package runs** (all inside the app container):

- PostHog web (Django, granian) and the Celery worker with its scheduler
- the Node plugin-server services: the CDP API that serves Hog function templates, event
  ingestion, session-replay blob ingestion, and the recording API
- the Rust fast path: `capture`, `replay-capture`, `feature-flags`, `property-defs-rs`,
  `personhog-replica` and `personhog-router`
- ClickHouse (with its built-in Keeper instead of ZooKeeper), Redpanda (Kafka), SeaweedFS
  (object storage) and Caddy as the single internal reverse proxy

PostgreSQL, Redis and mail come from the Cloudron addons. Everything is pinned to PostHog commit
`233686435f9b` and by image digest.

**Not included in 0.1.0** (upstream runs these as extra containers): Temporal and Elasticsearch
(workflows such as data warehouse syncs and batch exports), `livestream` (the live event feed),
`browserless` (heatmap screenshots), `cymbal` (error-tracking symbolication), the logs/traces/AI
capture services, CDP destination delivery (the cyclotron workers), and Apache Superset/embedded
dashboards.

**Signing in:** there is no Cloudron SSO. Self-hosted PostHog's OIDC support is a paid feature, so
the first account you create at the app's URL is the instance owner. A self-hosted instance cannot
create a second organisation, so use that account for everything.
manifest.changelog:
* First build: one container running web, worker, the node plugin-server services, capture,
  replay-capture, feature-flags, property-defs-rs, personhog-replica/router, ClickHouse (with
  built-in Keeper), Redpanda, SeaweedFS and Caddy
* PostgreSQL, Redis and mail from Cloudron addons
* Cloudron health check answers during the first-boot migrations
* ClickHouse data in a persistentDir, with a dump written into the backup (Cloudron backup crash
  workaround)
manifest.postInstallMessage:
## PostHog is installed

**Create the owner account.** Open the app and sign up. The first account becomes the instance
owner; self-hosted PostHog cannot create a second organisation, so keep this one.

Cloudron sign-in is not wired up: PostHog's OIDC/SAML support is an enterprise feature. Use the
email and password you set here, and keep it somewhere safe — there is no password reset by email
unless the mail addon is configured.

### Sending events

1. In **Project settings → Web snippet**, copy the project API key.
2. Point your site at this app:

   ```js
   posthog.init('<project-api-key>', {
     api_host: 'https://<this-app>',
     ui_host: 'https://<this-app>',
     person_profiles: 'identified_only'
   })
   ```

3. Events appear under **Activity → Live events** within a few seconds.

### First things to know

- **Analytics data lives in ClickHouse**, outside the ordinary `/app/data` backup folder, so its
  background merges cannot abort your whole server's backup run (a known Cloudron issue for any
  ClickHouse app). A dump of it is written into the backup at backup time; see the project README.
- **The first boot takes a while.** Migrations run before the services start; the app answers its
  health check immediately, so Cloudron will not time out. Expect tens of minutes on a fresh
  install, and check the app log for `[init] ready: services may start`.
- **Feature flags and session replay** work out of the box. **Data warehouse syncs, batch exports
  and CDP destination delivery are not included** in this version.

create-admin.message: Open the app and sign up: the first account becomes the instance owner. Self-hosted PostHog cannot create a second organisation, so use this account for everything.

storefront-snippet.message: In **Project settings → Web snippet**, copy the project API key into your site. Send browser events to this app's URL and set `ui_host` to the same URL.

manifest.changelog:
* Fix: declare the localstorage addon. Cloudron runs apps on a read-only filesystem and only this
  addon provides the writable /app/data the package needs; without it the app could not start.

manifest.changelog:
* Fix: ClickHouse backups. Version 26 refuses the Disk backup engine unless the disk is allowed
  explicitly, so every backup failed with "Code: 318. The 'backups.allowed_disk' configuration
  parameter is not set" and Cloudron's pre-update backup aborted the update.

manifest.changelog:
* Fix: backupCommand and restoreCommand run under /bin/sh, not bash, so the restore step silently did
  nothing with bash syntax. Both now re-exec themselves under bash.
* POSTINSTALL: sign-up needs the email-verification link (or a Web Terminal command when mail is off)
* docs/forum-post.md: the package's forum announcement
manifest.postInstallMessage:
## PostHog is installed

**Create the owner account.** Open the app and sign up. The first account becomes the instance
owner; self-hosted PostHog cannot create a second organisation, so keep this one.

Cloudron sign-in is not wired up: PostHog's OIDC/SAML support is an enterprise feature. Use the

**The sign-up sends a verification email.** With the sendmail addon configured, PostHog will not let

```
cd /code && set -a && . /run/posthog/env.sh && set +a
python manage.py shell -c "from posthog.models import User; u = User.objects.get(email='you@example.com'); u.is_email_verified = True; u.save()"
```
and then log in normally.

### Sending events

1. In **Project settings → Web snippet**, copy the project API key.
2. Point your site at this app:

   ```js
   posthog.init('<project-api-key>', {
     api_host: 'https://<this-app>',
     ui_host: 'https://<this-app>',
     person_profiles: 'identified_only'
   ```
